records.title: Provincial public-health emergency declaration
records.issuing_authority: Provincial Health Officer of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: Notice issued under the Public Health Act to exercise emergency information-collection powers.
records.neutral_summary: The Provincial Health Officer declared a public-health emergency after a sharp increase in drug-related overdoses and deaths.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The first progress report documents enhanced real-time reporting and response coordination.

records.title: First overdose-response progress update
records.issuing_authority: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
records.neutral_summary: The update documented initial emergency-response actions, data collection and the Joint Task Force.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Multiple measures were operational, while the broader emergency response continued.

records.title: January 2017 overdose-response progress update
records.issuing_authority: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
records.neutral_summary: A later progress update documented response activity and continuing mortality during the emergency.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The response had expanded, but the report recorded 914 deaths in 2016.
records.recurrence_notes: Continuing deaths are an outcome signal, not by themselves proof that any specific intervention failed.

records.title: Joint Task Force on Overdose Response
records.neutral_summary: The Province established a cross-sector task force to coordinate health and public-safety response measures.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The September progress report identifies the task force as established and coordinating initiatives.

records.title: 2018 illicit-drug overdose death review panel
records.neutral_summary: The panel recommended provincial oversight of treatment and recovery, expanded evidence-based addiction care including OAT and iOAT, and accessible provincial drug checking.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The 2022 panel stated that the 2017 panel recommendations remained relevant and required, while later sources document activity in each area.
records.recurrence_notes: The later panel repeated materially similar recommendations; this is a signal of unresolved work, not conclusive non-implementation.

records.title: Coroners' investigation findings on illicit-drug deaths
records.neutral_summary: The service published aggregate findings from completed 2016–2017 overdose death investigations, including prior health-system contact patterns.

records.title: Stopping the Harm recommendation
records.issuing_authority: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
records.neutral_summary: The PHO recommended an urgent public-health approach to possession and use in response to harms from the toxic illegal supply and criminalization.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: A time-limited federal exemption later changed possession enforcement in B.C., but did not implement the full public-health framework described in the report.

records.title: 2022 illicit-drug toxicity death review panel
records.neutral_summary: The panel recommended safer supply, a monitored 30/60/90-day action plan, and an evidence-based continuum of care.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Later official sources document a system-of-care framework, prescribed-alternatives policies, Road to Recovery and reporting, while the 2023 panel and 2024 audit identify continued gaps.
records.recurrence_notes: A 2023 death review panel again called for expanded alternatives to the unregulated supply.

records.title: Government and regulator responses to 2022 panel
records.issuing_authority: Ministries of Health and Mental Health and Addictions; health professional regulators
records.neutral_summary: The Coroners Service report index publishes response letters from responsible ministries and professional regulators.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The response documents describe intended and ongoing actions; they do not by themselves prove completion.
records.owner_review_reason: Commitment-level extraction from each response letter should be owner-reviewed before any completion claim.

records.title: Adult Substance Use System of Care Framework
records.neutral_summary: The technical policy framework describes core elements for an integrated, coordinated and evidence-based adult substance-use system.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Road to Recovery has subsequently been launched and expanded across several health-authority regions.

records.title: 2023 urgent-response death review panel
records.neutral_summary: The panel recommended additional measures to expand access to alternatives to the unregulated drug supply without requiring a prescription.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: No authoritative evidence of implementation of the non-prescriber model was located; later provincial policy remains prescription-based.
records.recurrence_notes: The recommendation followed earlier safer-supply recommendations and continuing toxic-drug deaths.
records.owner_review_reason: The subject is contested and the benchmark did not exhaust every possible exemption or pilot pathway.

records.title: PHO review of prescribed safer supply
records.issuing_authority: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
records.neutral_summary: The PHO reviewed B.C.'s prescribed safer supply initiative and issued recommendations for future action.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Government announced immediate updates in 2024 and published a revised prescribed-alternatives policy in 2025; recommendation-by-recommendation completion remains mixed.

records.title: Audit of OPS/SCS and prescribed safer supply implementation
records.issuing_authority: Office of the Auditor General of British Columbia
records.neutral_summary: The audit assessed ministry implementation of OPS/SCS and the first phase of prescribed safer supply and made recommendations on accountability, barriers and reporting.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The audit found operational programs alongside gaps in accountability, barriers and public performance reporting.
records.recurrence_notes: The audit provides authoritative evidence that implementation activity and unresolved gaps coexisted.

records.title: Ten-year toxic-drug response implementation inventory
records.neutral_summary: The Province summarized policy, professional-scope, treatment, harm-reduction and service actions undertaken since 2016.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The source confirms many discrete operational actions while describing an ongoing emergency.
records.recurrence_notes: Continuing mortality is documented but is not attributed to any single policy in this record.

records.title: Ministerial Order 488 requiring overdose prevention services
records.issuing_authority: Minister of Health of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: The order directed BC Emergency Health Services and regional health boards to provide overdose prevention services where needed during the emergency.
records.neutral_summary: The order created a provincial authority and duty pathway for emergency overdose prevention services.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: More than 20 sites had been established by January 2017.

records.title: Initial overdose prevention site rollout
records.issuing_authority: Government of British Columbia and regional health authorities
records.neutral_summary: Official reporting documented more than 20 sites and early visit and overdose-response activity.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The progress update reported sites operating in multiple communities.

records.title: Overdose Prevention Services Minimum Service Standards
records.binding_status_evidence: The document sets minimum expectations for publicly funded community and hospital OPS; exact enforceability depends on funding and operating arrangements.
records.neutral_summary: The provincial standards set consistent minimum requirements for fixed, mobile and hospital-based OPS.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The Province states the standards were implemented provincewide in 2025.

records.title: OPS/SCS provincial scale and utilization update
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported 58 sites as of September 2025 and aggregate visits and overdose responses through June 2025.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The official portal reports operational footprint and utilization; it does not establish causal population-level effectiveness.

records.title: Federal supervised-consumption authorization register
records.binding_status_evidence: Sites require a valid CDSA section 56.1 exemption and the register identifies authorized operating sites.
records.neutral_summary: Health Canada publishes current authorization and operating status for supervised consumption services.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The register provides site-level authorization and operational status.

records.title: Canada v. PHS Community Services Society
records.binding_status_evidence: Supreme Court of Canada judgment concerning the federal exemption decision for Insite.
records.neutral_summary: The Court ordered the Minister to grant the exemption needed for Insite to operate, on the record before it.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The judgment and subsequent federal site framework establish continuing legal relevance; this record does not generalize beyond the decision's scope.

records.title: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act exemption framework
records.binding_status_evidence: Federal statute governing controlled substances and exemption authorities, including supervised consumption.
records.neutral_summary: The CDSA establishes prohibitions and exemption mechanisms that shape treatment, drug checking and supervised consumption services.

records.title: Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act
records.binding_status_evidence: Federal statute amended the CDSA to provide specified charge protections when emergency help is sought for an overdose.
records.neutral_summary: The law provides limited protection from simple-possession charges and certain related breaches for people seeking or remaining with emergency assistance during an overdose.

records.title: Naloxone administration regulatory exception
records.issuing_authority: Minister of Health of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: B.C. Reg. 239/2016 amended the Health Professions General Regulation to permit emergency naloxone administration by otherwise unauthorized persons.
records.neutral_summary: The amendment removed a legal barrier to emergency naloxone administration outside hospital settings.

records.title: A Pathway to Hope strategy
records.neutral_summary: The ten-year roadmap set a provincial direction for mental-health and addictions service transformation.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Progress reporting documents completed and ongoing actions, while the strategy remains a long-term program.

records.title: A Pathway to Hope 2021 progress report
records.neutral_summary: Government reported more than half of plan items achieved and the remaining actions in implementation stages.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The report distinguishes achieved from ongoing plan items but does not resolve all later outcomes.

records.title: A Pathway to Hope 2019–2022 progress report
records.neutral_summary: The report documents service, standards, data and workforce activity over the first years of the strategy.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: It includes quantitative implementation indicators for OAT, OPS/SCS, prescribed alternatives, nurse prescribing and drug checking.

records.title: 2023 clinical guideline for opioid use disorder
records.issuing_authority: British Columbia Centre on Substance Use
records.neutral_summary: The provincial clinical guideline covers methadone, buprenorphine/naloxone and slow-release oral morphine and updates person-centred treatment guidance.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The pharmacy regulator aligned PPP-66 with the updated guideline on the same date.

records.title: Professional Practice Policy 66: Opioid Agonist Treatment
records.issuing_authority: College of Pharmacists of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: The regulator describes PPP-66 as requirements for pharmacists and pharmacy managers dispensing OAT.
records.neutral_summary: PPP-66 sets safe-dispensing requirements and aligns pharmacy practice with the provincial OUD guideline.

records.title: PPP-66 community health facility amendments
records.issuing_authority: College of Pharmacists of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: Regulator amendments allowed specified supply of OAT to community health facilities within exemption conditions.
records.neutral_summary: The amendments supported an integrated interdisciplinary OAT model in community health facilities.

records.title: Controlled-drug delivery standards
records.issuing_authority: College of Pharmacists of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: Standards were adopted in regulator bylaws and replaced PPP-71 on April 1, 2026.
records.neutral_summary: New standards cover delivery of controlled drug substances, including OAT, from community pharmacies and telepharmacies. The source identifies PPP-71 as the predecessor; that predecessor is not separately modeled in this fixture.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The regulator states the new standards took effect and replaced PPP-71.

records.title: Physician OAT training and practice requirements
records.issuing_authority: College of Physicians and Surgeons of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: CPSBC states mandatory training for specified OAT prescribing and links a practice standard; the page also includes advisory guidance.
records.neutral_summary: The regulator identifies OAT as a core substance-use competency and specifies training pathways for different medications.

records.title: NP prescribing standard for OUD and prescribed alternatives
records.issuing_authority: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives
records.binding_status_evidence: The practice standard is a bylaw under the Health Professions and Occupations Act.
records.neutral_summary: The standard sets education, preceptorship, clinical-guideline and evaluation conditions for nurse practitioner prescribing.

records.title: Certified RN opioid-use-disorder practice standard
records.issuing_authority: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives
records.binding_status_evidence: The bylaw standard defines certified-practice education, employer recognition, prescribing and continuity requirements.
records.neutral_summary: The standard authorizes qualified certified RNs to diagnose and treat OUD within specified limits and conditions.

records.title: Initial nurse OAT prescribing rollout
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported the first trained cohort of nurses beginning to prescribe OAT after a PHO order expanded scope during the emergency.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Later official reporting identified 226 nurses enrolled and 146 having completed the OAT stream by January 2023.

records.title: Provincial Opioid Treatment Access Line
records.neutral_summary: The Province launched a telephone service offering same-call clinical assessment, OAT prescribing when appropriate, and regional follow-up.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The official service announcement provides operating hours and care pathway.

records.title: Full PharmaCare coverage for OAT medications
records.neutral_summary: The Province reports that it began fully covering OAT medications under Plan Z for eligible B.C. residents.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The 2026 official timeline identifies the coverage change as implemented in 2023.

records.title: OAT participation and prescriber update
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported monthly OAT dispensing and prescriber counts for July 2024.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The factsheet documents service utilization and prescriber availability but does not establish unmet need or outcomes by itself.

records.title: Access to Prescribed Safer Supply policy direction
records.neutral_summary: The policy directed a phased expansion through health-authority and federally funded programs with monitoring and evaluation.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Programs operated and dispensed medications, while the Auditor General documented barriers and inadequate public performance reporting.
records.recurrence_notes: Later reviews identified operational activity and continued implementation gaps.

records.title: Prescribed safer supply implementation indicators
records.neutral_summary: The Pathway progress report provided dispensing counts, program phase information and clinical-protocol development activity.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The source shows service delivery at scale while describing a phased program still under development.

records.title: Government response to PHO safer-supply review
records.neutral_summary: Government announced immediate program updates and further policy work after the PHO review.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The response identifies changes initiated; it should not be treated as proof that every PHO recommendation was completed.

records.title: Access to Prescribed Alternatives policy
records.neutral_summary: The revised policy generally requires prescribed-alternative medication consumption in the presence of a health professional, subject to specified exceptions.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The Province states the new policy was published in 2025.
records.owner_review_reason: Supersession scope and practical service effects require document-level owner review.

records.title: Original B.C. personal-possession exemption
records.issuing_authority: Minister of Mental Health and Addictions and Associate Minister of Health (Canada)
records.binding_status_evidence: A CDSA subsection 56(1) exemption set conditions under which adults would not be arrested or charged for possession within the pilot.
records.neutral_summary: The three-year pilot exemption removed criminal penalties for qualifying adult personal possession up to a cumulative 2.5 grams, subject to exclusions.

records.title: September 2023 youth-area exemption amendment
records.binding_status_evidence: The federal exemption conditions were amended at B.C.'s request.
records.neutral_summary: The amendment added exclusions around designated youth-oriented outdoor areas.

records.title: May 2024 public-space exemption amendment
records.binding_status_evidence: Health Canada granted B.C.'s request to change the conditions of the CDSA exemption.
records.neutral_summary: The amendment restricted possession in public places while retaining the exemption in private residences, lawful sheltering places and designated health sites.

records.title: Provincial implementation summary after exemption amendment
records.neutral_summary: The Province summarized the narrowed possession framework alongside treatment and harm-reduction services.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The source confirms the changed locations where possession remained exempt and provides contemporaneous service counts.
records.owner_review_reason: The record documents implementation only; conclusions about effectiveness or causation require separate review.

records.title: Community Care and Assisted Living Act
records.binding_status_evidence: Provincial statute governing licensed community care and registered assisted living.
records.neutral_summary: The Act provides the statutory framework for registration, inspection and operating requirements relevant to supportive recovery residences.

records.title: Assisted Living Regulation — Supportive Recovery class
records.issuing_authority: Lieutenant Governor in Council of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: Provincial regulation establishes the Supportive Recovery class and mandatory operating requirements.
records.neutral_summary: The regulation requires overdose-response planning, accessible naloxone, staff training, resident information and medication policies for supportive recovery settings.

records.title: Registered Assisted Living Supportive Recovery Standards
records.neutral_summary: The standards expand on regulatory requirements with guidance on person-centred care, trauma-informed practice, programming and cultural safety.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Government publishes implementation resources and a training course for registered providers.

records.title: Residential Care Regulation — Substance Use class
records.issuing_authority: Lieutenant Governor in Council of British Columbia
records.binding_status_evidence: Provincial regulation establishes a Substance Use residential-care class and licensing requirements.
records.neutral_summary: The regulation governs licensed residential care for persons primarily in care due to substance dependence.

records.title: Mental Health Act framework relevant to concurrent substance-use care
records.binding_status_evidence: Provincial statute governs designated facilities, involuntary admission and treatment for persons meeting its mental-disorder criteria.
records.neutral_summary: The Act may govern care where statutory criteria are met; substance use alone should not be assumed to establish eligibility.
records.owner_review_reason: Application to addictions and concurrent disorders is fact-specific and must not be summarized as legal advice.

records.title: Public Health Act emergency and reporting framework
records.binding_status_evidence: Provincial statute defines PHO powers, public-health planning and reporting authorities.
records.neutral_summary: The Act supplied the legal framework invoked for the 2016 emergency declaration and PHO reporting.

records.title: Road to Recovery Vancouver launch and first beds
records.issuing_authority: Government of British Columbia and Providence Health Care
records.neutral_summary: The initial Vancouver model linked a centralized access line with detox, transition and treatment beds.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Thirty-four beds were operating; the full 95-bed configuration was scheduled for March 2025.

records.title: Provincewide Road to Recovery expansion commitment
records.neutral_summary: The Province committed nearly $154 million over three years for up to 100 beds, outpatient services and regional access lines.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Official 2026 reports document launches in several health-authority regions and named new services, but not full completion of every announced component.

records.title: Creekside withdrawal-management expansion
records.issuing_authority: Fraser Health and Government of British Columbia
records.neutral_summary: Fraser Health added ten medical withdrawal-management beds, transportation, Indigenous cultural-adviser capacity and a Hope RAAC satellite.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The health authority reports the beds and services as available and provides utilization and wait-time indicators.

records.title: VCH withdrawal-management program relocation
records.neutral_summary: VCH relocated 18 beds from Harbour Light to a new West 57th Avenue program and linked access through Access Central.

records.title: DTES Connections on-demand addiction clinic
records.neutral_summary: VCH opened a walk-in addiction clinic designed to provide rapid initiation and continuing addiction care.

records.title: Fraser Health 50-bed substance-use expansion
records.neutral_summary: Fraser Health reported 50 beds opened across named treatment, stabilization and supportive-recovery providers.

records.title: Maple Ridge youth treatment beds
records.issuing_authority: Fraser Health and Government of British Columbia
records.neutral_summary: Four withdrawal-management and treatment beds were added at Maple Ridge Treatment Centre for men aged 18–24.

records.title: 105 funded treatment and recovery beds operational
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported 105 newly funded beds fully operational through providers across all health-authority regions.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The announcement states the funded beds were operating and names the administering organization.

records.title: Budget 2023 treatment and recovery expansion
records.neutral_summary: Budget 2023 announced 100 community adult beds, a 95-bed seamless-care model, aftercare services and an Indigenous-led services fund.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Later sources document operating Road to Recovery components and additional bed totals, but candidate-level reconciliation of every Budget 2023 promise remains incomplete.
records.owner_review_reason: Headline bed totals may overlap across programs and fiscal announcements; reconciliation is required before completion claims.

records.title: Inlet Recovery Home service opening
records.issuing_authority: Island Health and Government of British Columbia
records.neutral_summary: A Port Alberni recovery service opened as part of Road to Recovery with a published access route.

records.title: Terrace Indigenous-led treatment and withdrawal-management expansion
records.issuing_authority: Government of British Columbia and partner First Nations organizations
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported a purchased withdrawal-management building in planning and commitments for treatment, supportive-recovery and aftercare capacity.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Property acquisition and planning are evidenced; the announced new capacity should not yet be treated as operational.

records.title: First Nations-led beds in Adams Lake, Skidegate and Old Massett
records.issuing_authority: Government of British Columbia, First Nations Health Authority and community partners
records.neutral_summary: Twelve First Nations-led treatment and supportive-recovery beds opened in three communities.

records.title: FNHA-funded treatment centre evaluation 2018–2023
records.neutral_summary: The Indigenous-led evaluation describes the funded network, rapid-access beds, specialized referrals and access barriers.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The report confirms operational services and rapid-access arrangements while documenting capacity and access constraints.
records.recurrence_notes: High demand and waitlists are documented as continuing access concerns.

records.title: Expert Task Force recommendations on alternatives to criminal penalties
records.issuing_authority: Health Canada Expert Task Force on Substance Use
records.neutral_summary: The task force recommended ending criminal penalties for simple possession and addressing related health and social supports.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: B.C.'s exemption provided a limited, time-bound implementation in one province; Canada did not implement the recommendation nationally.

records.title: Expert Task Force recommendations on federal drug strategy
records.issuing_authority: Health Canada Expert Task Force on Substance Use
records.neutral_summary: The task force recommended a public-health framework, safer-supply expansion, ongoing funding, equity and national service standards.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The renewed CDSS adopted an integrated health-oriented strategy and planned regulatory changes, but did not implement every task-force recommendation.
records.recurrence_notes: Several themes recur in later coroner and public-health recommendations.

records.title: Federal response to Expert Task Force reports
records.neutral_summary: The Minister acknowledged the reports and stated that the recommendations were under review and would inform next steps.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The statement is evidence of consideration, not implementation.

records.title: Renewed Canadian Drugs and Substances Strategy
records.neutral_summary: The renewed federal strategy organizes action around prevention, services and supports, evidence and substance controls, with monitoring commitments.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: Federal action summaries and project registers document ongoing initiatives; strategy-wide outcomes remain under evaluation.

records.title: Horizontal evaluation of the Canadian Drugs and Substances Strategy
records.issuing_authority: Health Canada Office of Audit and Evaluation
records.neutral_summary: The evaluation assessed the strategy and includes a management response and action plan.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The management response records accepted actions and planned timelines; completion must be assessed against later deliverables.

records.title: Federal safer-supply pilot early findings
records.neutral_summary: A commissioned qualitative assessment summarized early implementation learning from ten federally funded projects, including B.C. programs.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The evaluation confirms funded pilots were delivering medications and wraparound services; it was an early qualitative assessment, not a full outcome evaluation.

records.title: Provincial distributed drug-checking service
records.neutral_summary: The Province began a model allowing rural and remote sample collection and transport under a federal exemption.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The Pathway progress report documents launch and operating model.

records.title: Drug-checking site coverage update
records.neutral_summary: The Province reported 128 access sites, split between on-site devices and off-site testing pathways.
records.implementation_evidence_summary: The source gives a current service-coverage count but not a needs-based geographic adequacy assessment.

records.title: High-Risk Drinking and Alcohol Use Disorder guideline
records.neutral_summary: The provincial guideline supports identification and management of high-risk drinking and alcohol use disorder in adults and youth.

commitments.title: Regulate and oversee treatment and recovery programs
commitments.summary: Create provincial regulation and oversight so treatment and recovery facilities provide evidence-based care and report outcomes.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Assisted-living regulation and supportive-recovery standards address parts of the recommendation; the 2022 panel said the earlier recommendation remained relevant and required.
commitments.owner_review_reason: The extent to which the regulatory regime fully satisfies the panel recommendation is interpretive.

commitments.title: Expand OAT and iOAT access
commitments.summary: Expand evidence-based addiction care across the continuum, including oral and injectable opioid agonist treatment.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Nurse prescribing, updated professional standards, PharmaCare coverage and the OAT access line are documented; adequacy and iOAT reach were not established.

commitments.title: Create accessible provincial drug checking
commitments.summary: Create accessible provincial drug-checking services using validated technologies.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: A distributed service launched in 2021 and the Province later reported 128 access sites.

commitments.title: Ensure access to a safer supply
commitments.summary: Ensure a safer drug supply for people at risk of dying from the toxic unregulated supply.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Prescription-based programs operated, but the Auditor General documented access barriers and the 2023 panel sought broader non-prescriber access.

commitments.title: Publish a monitored 30/60/90-day action plan
commitments.summary: Develop and publish a time-bound illicit-drug-toxicity action plan with ongoing monitoring.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Related frameworks and action inventories were located, but no official document clearly matching the requested 30/60/90-day plan was confirmed.
commitments.owner_review_reason: A similarly named internal or archived plan may exist; absence was not exhaustively proven.

commitments.title: Establish an evidence-based continuum of care
commitments.summary: Build an accountable substance-use continuum including screening, treatment, recovery and workforce supports.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The Adult System of Care Framework and multi-region Road to Recovery services are documented; full provincewide operationalization was not demonstrated.

commitments.title: Explore non-prescribed alternatives to the toxic supply
commitments.summary: Pursue a model allowing access to regulated alternatives without an individual prescription.
commitments.originating_organization: BC Coroners Service Death Review Panel
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The benchmark found no authoritative evidence of a non-prescriber model; later provincial policy remained prescription-based.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Contested policy area and possible narrow pilots or exemptions require deeper verification.

commitments.title: Remove criminal penalties for personal possession
commitments.summary: Use a public-health rather than criminal-law approach to personal possession in B.C.
commitments.originating_organization: Office of the Provincial Health Officer
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: A time-limited federal exemption took effect in 2023 and was materially narrowed in 2024.

commitments.title: Phase in prescribed safer supply
commitments.summary: Implement prescribed alternatives through existing health-authority programs, service hubs, outreach teams and federally funded projects.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Official progress reporting confirms dispensing and programs; the audit found persistent barriers and inadequate public performance reporting.

commitments.title: Monitor and evaluate prescribed safer supply
commitments.summary: Collect and publish evidence to guide later phases and clinical guidance.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Internal monitoring and external reviews existed, but the Auditor General found public reporting inadequate and planned data had not been published.

commitments.title: Address barriers to prescribed-alternatives implementation
commitments.summary: Develop clearer collaborative strategies to address prescriber, medication, rural and remote access barriers.
commitments.originating_organization: Office of the Auditor General of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: A revised policy was issued, but a later completion audit was not located.

commitments.title: Improve public performance reporting
commitments.summary: Report implementation and performance against OPS/SCS and prescribed-alternatives program objectives.
commitments.originating_organization: Office of the Auditor General of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: Ministry of Mental Health and Addictions
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Later government inventories provide activity counts, but the benchmark did not locate a recommendation-specific completion report.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Activity reporting may not meet the audit's performance-reporting criteria; owner interpretation is required.

commitments.title: Build a comprehensive mental-health and addictions system
commitments.summary: Shift from a fragmented crisis response toward prevention, early intervention and coordinated care.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Successive progress reports document activity; the ten-year horizon has not elapsed.

commitments.title: Add up to 100 Road to Recovery beds
commitments.summary: Expand Road to Recovery with up to 100 new substance-use beds over three years.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Named services and beds opened in several regions, but the benchmark did not reconcile all openings to the promised 100.

commitments.title: Create a substance-use access line in each health-authority region
commitments.summary: Provide a single regional access route for assessment, planning and treatment connection.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Access Central is operational in Vancouver, Fraser and Island Health sources; full five-region verification was not completed.

commitments.title: Create 100 community adult treatment and recovery beds
commitments.summary: Fund 100 new publicly funded adult community treatment and recovery beds with no fees for B.C. residents.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Later aggregate bed counts rose and named services opened, but no authoritative one-to-one reconciliation of the specific 100-bed commitment was located.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Possible double counting across fiscal announcements and Road to Recovery requires owner reconciliation.

commitments.title: Implement a 95-bed seamless-care model
commitments.summary: Launch a linked 95-bed pathway spanning detox, transition, treatment and recovery.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Initial beds and Access Central were operational; the benchmark did not locate a later source confirming the full 95-bed configuration by the stated date.
commitments.owner_review_reason: The expected date passed and a full configuration count was not confirmed in the inspected sources.

commitments.title: Invest $171 million in Indigenous-led services
commitments.summary: Fund Indigenous-led treatment, recovery and aftercare services.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Official sources document specific First Nations-led openings and projects, while full fund-level reconciliation was not completed.

commitments.title: Operate 105 funded treatment and recovery beds
commitments.summary: Make 105 newly funded treatment and recovery beds available through providers across the province.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: Canadian Mental Health Association BC Division
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The Province reported all 105 beds fully operational.

commitments.title: Open 123 youth substance-use beds
commitments.summary: Expand youth treatment and withdrawal-management capacity by 123 beds across B.C.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The inspected source confirms four Maple Ridge beds as part of the wider commitment; full 123-bed reconciliation was not located.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Only a subset of the announced provincial total was individually verified.

commitments.title: Launch a provincewide same-day OAT line
commitments.summary: Provide a provincial telephone pathway for same-call clinical assessment and OAT initiation when appropriate.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The official launch provides the operating number, hours and clinical pathway.

commitments.title: Enable trained nurses to prescribe OAT
commitments.summary: Expand the qualified prescriber workforce by authorizing trained RNs and RPNs within specified conditions.
commitments.originating_organization: Provincial Health Officer of British Columbia
responsible_organizations: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives
British Columbia Centre on Substance Use
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Training cohorts began prescribing in 2021 and the regulator now has an in-force certified-practice standard.

commitments.title: Implement provincewide OPS minimum standards
commitments.summary: Apply consistent quality, accessibility and cultural-safety expectations to publicly funded community and hospital OPS.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Government states the standards were implemented provincewide in 2025.

commitments.title: End criminal penalties for simple possession
commitments.summary: Remove criminal penalties and coercive measures for simple possession across Canada.
commitments.originating_organization: Health Canada Expert Task Force on Substance Use
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The B.C. exemption was a limited provincial pilot and was narrowed; no national implementation was found.

commitments.title: Establish national substance-use service standards
commitments.summary: Define national standards for harm reduction, treatment, recovery and other supports.
commitments.originating_organization: Health Canada Expert Task Force on Substance Use
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The renewed CDSS supports service access but the benchmark did not locate a binding or comprehensive national standards instrument.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Multiple professional and program standards exist; the task-force concept may not map to a single instrument.

commitments.title: Create a clearer federal authorization process
commitments.summary: Develop a regulatory authorization pathway for supervised consumption, urgent public-health-need sites and drug checking.
commitments.originating_organization: Health Canada
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: Health Canada continues to administer exemptions and a public status register; completion of the proposed regulatory scheme was not confirmed.
commitments.owner_review_reason: Current statutory and forthcoming regulatory pathways require legal-version review before a completion finding.

commitments.title: Build Terrace treatment, supportive-recovery and aftercare capacity
commitments.summary: Add 12 treatment beds, 10 supportive-recovery beds, an aftercare hub and a community withdrawal-management site.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia and Northern First Nations Alliance
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: A building purchase and planning are confirmed; the new beds and hub were not yet described as open.

commitments.title: Open 12 First Nations-led treatment and recovery beds
commitments.summary: Open four treatment beds in Adams Lake and four supportive-recovery beds in each of Skidegate and Old Massett.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia and First Nations partners
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The official announcement describes the beds as opening and available in the three communities.

commitments.title: Publish a revised prescribed-alternatives policy
commitments.summary: Update provincial prescribed-alternatives requirements after the PHO review.
commitments.originating_organization: Government of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: The Province states a new policy was published in 2025.

commitments.title: Provide overdose prevention services where needed
commitments.summary: Require BC Emergency Health Services and regional health boards to provide rapid overdose-prevention services during the emergency where need is identified.
commitments.originating_organization: Minister of Health of British Columbia
commitments.implementation_evidence_summary: More than 20 sites were operating within weeks, with later growth documented.
